concept.name: Consensus mechanism
concept.definition: A consensus mechanism is the complete stack of protocols, incentives and ideas that allows a distributed network of nodes to agree on a single state of a blockchain, including Sybil resistance, block author selection and a chain-selection (fork-choice) rule.
concept.intuition: It is the rulebook that lets thousands of strangers agree on one version of history without a referee.
concept.mechanics: A Sybil-resistance component (e.g. proof-of-work's energy expenditure or proof-of-stake's locked capital) makes it costly to fake identities; a block-production protocol selects who proposes and validates blocks; and a fork-choice rule (longest/heaviest chain) resolves competing versions. Economic rewards and penalties align honest behavior.
concept.failure_modes: If an attacker obtains 51% of hash power or a large share of stake, they can censor or reorder transactions and, below finality thresholds, reorganize the chain; bugs in the fork-choice rule can cause chain splits.
concept.misconceptions: Proof-of-work and proof-of-stake alone are not complete consensus mechanisms — they are Sybil-resistance and block-author-selection components inside one (e.g. Ethereum's Gasper combines Casper-FFG with LMD-GHOST).
concept.example: On Ethereum, consensus is reached when validators representing at least two-thirds of total staked ETH attest to checkpoint blocks, at which point those checkpoints are justified and then finalized.
